claims.text_en: The MRT Phra Ram 9 station (code BL20) opened on 3 July 2004 on the Blue Line as an underground station at the junction of Ratchadaphisek, Rama IX, Din Daeng and Asok-Din Daeng roads, spanning Din Daeng and Huai Khwang districts, with exits 1-3, an underground-mall level and a walkway into Central Rama 9's basement floor.

geography.notes: The station is the unit's anchor. The app's context line says 'BL23?' which disagrees with Wikipedia's BL20 - flagged in open_issues, no score impact.

temporal_scope.notes: Station code taken from the current Wikipedia infobox.

evidence.paraphrase: Station BL20, opened 3 July 2004; located in Din Daeng and Huai Khwang districts at the junction of Din Daeng, Asok-Din Daeng, Ratchadaphisek and Rama IX roads; B1 holds exits 1-3 and the underground mall with a walkway to Central Rama 9's B floor.

limitations: Community-edited encyclopedia; details re-extracted twice with consistent results.

claims.text_en: Central GR9, the mall renamed from CentralPlaza Grand Rama 9 (opened 14 December 2011, nine storeys), connects directly to the station via an underground tunnel, and its anchors have included Robinson (operating as such until 27 November 2025), Tops Food Hall, Tops Daily, SFX Cinemas, PowerBuy, SuperSports and Fitness First.

geography.notes: Mall block at the Rama IX Road address 9/9, opposite Fortune Town; inside the catchment per its tunnel connection to the station.

temporal_scope.notes: Anchor list captures the Nov 2025-2026 transition (Robinson ceased as Robinson 2025-11-27).

evidence.paraphrase: Renamed Central GR9; opened 2011-12-14; underground connection to Phra Ram 9 MRT station; anchors list Robinson until 27 Nov 2025, Tops Food Hall, Tops Daily, SFX, PowerBuy, SuperSports, Fitness First.
Underground walkway to B floor of Central Rama 9.

limitations: Wikipedia article itself flagged for over-reliance on primary sources.
Uniqlo (verified separately, phra-ram-9-c09) is absent from the anchor list.

claims.text_en: Central Pattana's Central GR9 'Future District' programme integrates the Central Rama 9 shopping centre with three office towers (G Tower, R House - formerly Unilever House - and The Ninth Tower) across 73 rai and about 1.1 million sq m of gross building area, with retail transformation under way and a phased reopening beginning in early 2028 as part of a THB 110 billion 2026-2030 investment plan.

geography.notes: Block behind/around the existing mall at the Rama 9 junction.

temporal_scope.notes: Announced 2026-03-26; reopening dates are the developer's own projections.

evidence.paraphrase: Central GR9 is a mixed-use 'Future District' spanning 73 rai / 1.1 million sq m GBA integrating Central Rama 9 with G Tower, R House (formerly Unilever House) and The Ninth Tower; retail phased reopening beginning early 2028; part of a THB 110 billion 2026-2030 plan.
Grand Rama 9 project folds Central Rama 9, G Tower, R House and The Ninth Tower into a 73-rai, ~1.1 million sq m plan; retail reopening reportedly from early 2028.

limitations: Developer's own announcement (commercial context); independent confirmation of the phasing schedule not yet available.

claims.text_en: The Jodd Fairs night market, which opened in November 2021 on leased land behind Central Rama 9 with roughly 600-800 stalls, closed permanently in January 2025 when the lease on the plot ended and the site was handed back for redevelopment.

geography.notes: Site directly behind the mall on the Rama 9 side; inside the catchment.

temporal_scope.notes: Closure month confirmed by three independent guides; the exact final trading day was not pinned.

evidence.paraphrase: Rama 9 market opened November 2021 on land leased from G Land and closed for good in January 2025 after the lease expired; the plot was handed back for redevelopment, with a two-month overlap with the new site.
Lease with Central expires December 2023; 700-800 stalls to be relocated; land returned to Central Group, reported plan for a 125-storey 'Super Tower'.
Update January 2026: 'Jodd Fairs Rama 9 is permanently closed'; successor beside Big C Place Ratchadaphisek.

limitations: The 2023 plan (move January 2024) slipped; sources agree the site traded until January 2025.

question_answers.notes: Identity: MRT Phra Ram 9, Blue Line, code BL20 (app says 'BL23?' - discrepancy flagged, not scored). Administrative unit spans Din Daeng and Huai Khwang districts. Physical stop at the Ratchadaphisek/Rama IX/Din Daeng/Asok-Din Daeng junction. Named corridors: Ratchadaphisek and Rama IX roads. Inside: Central GR9 mall (tunnel-connected). Station-corner: Fortune Town. Outside: Jodd Fairs Ratchada successor market. Partial: Pracha Rat Bamphen 'New Chinatown' strip, RCA edge, SET on the corridor. Final polygon membership (Piyavate, RCA, SET, Fortune Town) is deferred to the coordinator's geometry check per brief rules.

Whose experience: weekday office workers and MRT commuters dominate (guide-reported tenant base); evenings belong to the corridor's entertainment zones rather than the station block itself. The 'new CBD' self-image (developers, agents) shapes the area's marketed identity; guide authors flag that the re-rating is already priced in.

Valued mechanisms: one-stop complex (tunnel-linked mall + offices + MRT), mall groceries/dining/gyms, mainstream retail (UNIQLO), cheap-and-local electronics (Fortune Town - guide opinion, not a price survey), a private international hospital on the corridor, and job density from the office cluster. Guide opinion vs verified fact is separated per claim limitations.

Deliberate counter-evidence: adult-leaning entertainment layer (soapy massage venues described as prostitution fronts; 02:00 RCA licensing), no significant public park in the core, current asking rents above the app's baseline (14,000 vs ~21,900 1BR average), and recurring junction congestion. No explicit area-wide crime warning surfaced; app safety=5 not independently validated.

Weekday daytime peaks from offices; the big evening night-market pull moved one stop north (successor market, 1 Nov 2024 opening, outside the unit); RCA runs latest (02:00); weekend focus shifts to the malls and the one-stop-away market. Seasonal variation not covered by sources read.

Verified station hardware: exits 1-3, underground-mall level, tunnel/walkway into Central GR9's basement. Most tenants reportedly commute by MRT; junction traffic congestion is a recurring complaint. No sidewalk-quality or crossing audit was performed (no field visit); no walking durations were derived from the 800 m radius - distances stated instead.

Groceries: Tops Food Hall and Tops Daily inside Central GR9 (Big C Extra on the corridor per Wikivoyage, one stop north). Ordinary food: mall food court/patio plus Fortune Town area. Gyms: Fitness First anchor in the mall. Healthcare: Piyavate international hospital on Rama 9 Road (polygon membership unverified).

Asking (not signed) rents: 1BR average ~21,900, 2BR ~37,000 THB, wide ranges; rents reported up 8-14% in a year while sale prices flat. The brief's 30,000/60,000 lead matches the premium/new-supply end (Belle Grand two-beds 30,400-52,000; 3BR average ~61,000), not the median. Sample limits: live listings, portal-defined area, commercial context.

What is actually inside: no named public park found in any source read; greenery is mostly private (mall/condo landscaping). Public park access is by train (Benjakitti ~7 min, Chatuchak ~15 min per the guide). Suan Luang Rama IX is a naming trap - half an hour away. App green=7 is not reconciled with this and needs the coordinator's park-hectare check.

Conditional fit: strong for MRT-first professionals, couples and singles who want office proximity and mall convenience; poor for families needing schools (thin layer) and for anyone prioritizing parks or quiet streets; night-owl visitors are served one stop away, not in-unit. No universal 'best-area' claim is made.

Recent changes: Jodd Fairs Rama 9 closed January 2025 (site handed back), successor opened 1 Nov 2024 outside the unit; mall renamed Central GR9 with Robinson ceasing as Robinson 27 Nov 2025; GR9 retail phased reopening from early 2028 (developer projection; a circulating '20 May 2026 opening' date appears to conflate Central Khon Kaen Campus); Orange Line late-2027 projection; Grey Line monorail planned without a date.

Uncertainties: asking vs signed rents (app baseline below current asking averages); GR9 timeline churn (developer projections only); stale map coordinates still pointing at the demolished market; no park inside despite green=7; station-code mismatch (app BL23? vs Wikipedia BL20); 'crowd=2' semantics unverified; a Reddit thread asking whether the New CBD project failed could not be accessed (403) and remains an unexamined community view.

editorial.preview: Since Jodd Fairs Rama 9 closed in January 2025 and its successor opened beside Thailand Cultural Centre MRT about two kilometres away, the station's famous night-market anchor now sits outside this unit - leaving a mall mid-transition, offices and higher asking rents behind.
editorial.guide_lead: Phra Ram 9 is the Blue Line stop (BL20, since 2004) where Bangkok's self-styled second CBD concentrates: G Tower, AIA Capital Center and the former Unilever House around a junction served by a tunnel-linked mall. That mall, renamed Central GR9, is mid-redevelopment - Robinson closed in November 2025 and Central Pattana projects phased retail reopening from early 2028. The area's best-known evening draw, Jodd Fairs, closed in January 2025 and now trades one MRT stop north, so late-night energy lives on the corridor rather than in the catchment. Daily life is mall-shaped (Tops Food Hall, UNIQLO, Fitness First, Fortune Town electronics) with a private international hospital on Rama 9 Road, but no named public park inside the unit. Asking rents have moved well above the app's 14,000/29,500 THB references, averaging about 21,900 (1BR) and 37,000 THB (2BR) on listing portals.

strengths.text_en: One-stop complex: a tunnel-connected mall with groceries, cinema and gym stacked directly over the MRT station since 2004.
Job density: a corporate cluster (G Tower, AIA, R House, The Ninth Towers) plus the SET on the corridor, which is what keeps weekday demand - and rental yields - resilient.
Ordinary-errands layer inside the catchment: Tops Food Hall/Daily, UNIQLO, Fortune Town's local-priced electronics, and Piyavate international hospital on the Rama 9 corridor.
Rail upside is real but dated: Orange Line civil works complete with a late-2027 opening projection, and a planned Grey monorail interchange on the M-Map.

tradeoffs.text_en: The demolition aftermath is measurable: the unit lost its anchor night market in January 2025 and its replacement sits about two kilometres away on the same corridor.
The app's rent references now read as entry-level: asking averages run about 21,900 THB (1BR) and 37,000 THB (2BR), with rents up 8-14 per cent in a year while sale prices sat flat.
No significant public park exists in the core - green access is a train ride to Benjakitti or Chatuchak, and tree-lined private landscaping is not park access.

The corridor's entertainment layer is adult-leaning - 02:00-licensed RCA clubs, Soi 4 pubs and soapy massage venues described as prostitution fronts - which families may weigh differently than singles.
Construction-over-convenience: the mall itself is a worksite-to-2028 transition zone, with Robinson already gone since November 2025.

day_night.text_en: Weekdays are office-shaped: daytime peaks around the towers and the mall food floors, with most residents commuting by MRT and congestion at the junction as the counter-rhythm.
Evenings: the mall and cinema stay local, while the night-market crowd now flows one stop north to Jodd Fairs Ratchada and later-night drinkers head to RCA (licensed to 02:00).
Weekends centre on the mall and mall-adjacent dining; the unit itself has no market square since January 2025.

within_area_variation.text_en: The mall-office blocks at the junction (tunnel level, plaza towers) contrast with the older soi fringes off Ratchadaphisek, where low-rise room stock and entry rents (~15,000 THB 1BR examples) still exist.
The former Jodd Fairs plot behind the mall is now handed-back redevelopment land inside the unit, while its trading successor sits outside it - the unit's busiest footnote is a construction site.
Green and quiet tilt to the edges and beyond: nothing named inside, Benjakitti and Chatuchak by train, RCA noise at the southern rim.

conditional_fit.text_en: Best fit: MRT-first professionals, couples and singles who value office proximity and a one-stop complex over parks and schools - the guide-reported tenant base.
Poor fit: families prioritizing schools (thin international layer) and green-space-led lifestyles (no core park).
Nightlife-first residents are served by the corridor (successor market one stop north, RCA late licensing) rather than by anything in-unit after January 2025.
Chinese-food daily life is a corridor habit (Pracha Rat Bamphen's mainland restaurants) more than an in-unit feature; expect a stop on the MRT rather than a stroll.

uncertainties: GR9's retail reopening schedule rests on the developer's own March 2026 announcement (phased reopening from early 2028); a conflicting 'opens 20 May 2026' claim in circulation appears to describe Central Khon Kaen Campus instead.
All rent figures are asking prices from a listing portal whose 'Phra Ram 9' area definition may exceed the app's 800 m polygon; signed-contract rents were not available.
Whether the UNIQLO store continues trading through the GR9 transition could not be re-verified beyond a 2013 directory record plus the brand's locator.
Polygon membership is unverified for Piyavate Hospital, RCA, SET, Fortune Town and the successor market; the coordinator's geometry check should settle these.
The station code in the app ('BL23?') disagrees with Wikipedia's BL20; no operator source was consulted to arbitrate.
The app's crowd=2 and safety=5 encodings were not independently validated; no crime statistics were read, only guide-level cautions.
A Reddit thread asking whether the Rama 9 New CBD project failed returned HTTP 403 and remains an unexamined counter-view.
No field visit was made; sidewalk, crossing and podium-level walkability claims are limited to the tunnel/exit facts already sourced.

open_issues: Station code mismatch: app says 'BL23?' while Wikipedia lists BL20 - verify against an MRTA/BEM operator page before publication.

Central GR9 opening-date conflict in secondary circulation (20 May 2026 vs phased reopening from early 2028); the Central Group newsroom release read here supports the 2028 phasing - re-check CPN channels for post-November 2026 updates.
Reddit r/Bangkok thread 'Is Rama 9 New CBD project a failure?' inaccessible (HTTP 403); community counter-view on the CBD narrative uncaptured.

Thai news coverage of the Jodd Fairs closure (Brand Inside, Bangkok Biz News, Prachachat surfaced in discovery) could not be pinned to stable URLs; Thai-language sourcing for the closure date therefore indirect.
Academic study on the 'New Chinatown' (Huai Khwang/Ratchada) surfaced in search but was not retrievable (rate limit); would strengthen the community-layer claim.

Coordinator tasks: polygon checks for Fortune Town, Piyavate Hospital, RCA, SET, Pracha Rat Bamphen strip and the successor market site; verify app's mapped park hectares against the no-core-park finding.
Signed-rent data (as opposed to asking) for 2025-2026 not found from an open source; rent baseline remains asking-price-based.
Sidewalk/crossing quality and entrance congestion around exits 1-3 not audited (no field observation); statements limited to sourced tunnel/exit facts.
